_comment: Skills whose newest probing report is KNOWN to be a weak measurement -- it covered only a SUBSET of the skill's positive cases (P006), or it covered them and the skill did not fire (P007) -- and whose weakness the program has ADJUDICATED and decided to carry. Read by skills/skill-authoring/scripts/case_coverage.py. An entry silences P006 and P007 for that skill; P008 is this file's own rot check. The reason this is a baseline rather than a hard failure is the reason P004 has one: the fix is a RE-PROBE, which costs live model calls (~$0.05/probe), so a check that can only go green by spending money is a check a round will uninstall. Required fields: `owner` (the track that will pay), `why`, and `report` -- the CONTENT PIN, the exact report basename the acknowledgement was made against (round 373's pattern in state/known-escalated-diffs.json). P008 ERRORS: the skill is not in the corpus; no `owner`; the skill now covers all its positive cases with full recall (an acknowledgement that outlives its debt is a mute button, case_coverage's P005 rule); or the pinned report is no longer the newest one holding a probe of it, which means someone re-probed and did not re-adjudicate. `measured`/`positives` are recorded as a fact-at-the-time so a reader can see whether the number moved; they are NOT asserted, because pinning a live aggregate is round 340's fake-regression trap.

obligation-ledger.why: RE-ADJUDICATED by round 381 and the old verdict was WRONG. The entry used to read 'probed 1/3 in the same round and 0/3 on the re-probe after a description edit ... a skill whose own subject is a two-part process rule currently fails to fire on its own trigger cases'. Round 381 re-probed all three positives at the FULL 41-skill corpus at n=3 (round-381-armJ.json): ol-near 3/3, ol-far 3/3, ol-mid 0/3 -- 6 of 9, not 0 of 3. Staged ALONE (round-381-ol-isolation.json) it is 9/9. What survives is ONE case, ol-mid, at 0/3 across two independent runs; what does not survive is 'the description does not fire'. The entry stays because ol-mid is a real, replicated per-case miss, NOT because the description is known-bad.
obligation-ledger.measured: 6/9 recall at the full corpus (ol-near 3/3, ol-far 3/3, ol-mid 0/3); 9/9 staged alone

policy-replay-over-history.why: 3 of 4 with 100% precision (round 369). The single miss, prh-audit, fired NOTHING rather than firing a competitor -- round 369's chose-nothing shape, which it measured across three corpus sizes and showed is not a corpus-size effect. Kept unedited: one case at n=1 is a draw, not a description defect, which is round 357's finding replicated. The right next move is a repeat of prh-audit at n>=4, not a rewrite. ROUND 381: still unrepeated -- the prh-audit repeat at n>=4 was displaced by this round's instrument work and remains owed. Round 381's finding makes the repeat MORE valuable, not less: prh-audit's single miss is exactly the one-draw shape that this round showed can be 0/12 and 12/12 for the same configuration.

derived-subject-set.why: REFUTED, not unmeasured, and one edit has already been tried and scored. Round 393 probed all three positives as 3 separate runs x 2 repeats (round-393-run{A,B,C}.json): 2 of 18, Wilson 95% [0.03, 0.33] -- the interval lies entirely below a coin flip, and the skill fired ZERO times in runs A and B. It loses to a different competitor almost every time (declaration-scope-parity, unenforced-documented-rule, citation-registry-integrity, fuzz-mutate-kill-loop) rather than to one consistent sibling, which is the signature of a description that stakes no claim rather than one that overlaps a neighbour. Round 393 then made ONE edit -- leading with the hand-written-list mechanism instead of gating on 'an anti-rot test is green', and naming the three displacing skills in the NOT clauses -- and re-probed it the same way (round-393-dss-run{D,E,F}.json): 0 of 18. THE EDIT MADE IT WORSE AND WAS REVERTED; the description on disk is round 392's. Round 141's stop-rule applies: no second edit without new information. The sharpest single datum for whoever picks this up is dss-near-2, the MODULES-tuple case and the cleanest instance of the skill, which ABSTAINED 6 of 6 post-edit even though the edited description contained that exact scenario almost verbatim -- quoting a case's own words into a description is not what makes it select. RE-PINNED by round 405, verdict UNCHANGED. Round 405 did not probe this skill's own positive cases; it appears in round-405-run{A,B,C,D}.json only through `fsd-neg-list`, a crossing negative owned by filter-shares-the-defect that expects THIS skill -- 1 of 5. That is consistent with 2/18 and adds nothing, so the adjudication above stands and only the content pin moved (P008 exists to force exactly this re-reading rather than let a stale pin ride). One NEW datum from round 405's displacement matrix, which is the first thing in this repo to ask what BEATS a losing skill: across the archive this skill's losses go to declaration-scope-parity (3), unenforced-documented-rule (3) and citation-registry-integrity (2) with a top-taker share of 18%, and 10 of 18 of its losses were ABSTENTIONS -- nothing fired at all. Round 393 called that 'the signature of a description that stakes no claim rather than one that overlaps a neighbour' and round 405 measured it corpus-wide. The remedy that follows is a concrete mechanism no neighbour could also claim, NOT another contrast clause; round 393's one reverted edit was a contrast clause.
derived-subject-set.measured: 2/18 pooled over 3 runs, Wilson [0.03, 0.33]; 0/18 after one reverted edit; 1/5 on fsd-neg-list in round 405; 10 of 18 archive losses were abstentions

repeats-are-not-replicates.why: Authored AND probed by round 393, which is the round's own paraphrase scoring its own wording (round 357 item 3's independence concern) -- recorded, not hidden. 12 of 18 pooled over 3 separate runs x 2 repeats (round-393-rnr-run{A,B,C}.json), Wilson 95% [0.44, 0.84]: UNDECIDED, like 28 other skills in this corpus. What makes it worth an entry rather than a shrug is that the miss is NOT a run effect: rnr-far and rnr-mid fired 2/2 in every run and rnr-near fired 0/2 in EVERY run, so the per-case pattern is stable and rnr-near is a real boundary problem, not a draw -- the exact distinction this skill exists to make, applied to itself. rnr-near loses to `rerun-before-you-record` (2 of 6) or abstains (4 of 6), and the overlap is honest: that skill's subject is 'run it again before you record the verdict' and rnr-near's prompt is a re-run that disagreed. The negative case rnr-neg-selection ALSO false-fired 6 of 6 (this skill 2, rerun-before-you-record 3, freshness-is-not-outcome 2), and the case may simply be mis-authored: selection-on-outcome IS step 5 of this skill, so `expect: []` is arguable. NO EDIT HAS BEEN MADE. Round 141's stop-rule budget is untouched, and the next round to pick this up should decide the rnr-near / rerun-before-you-record boundary as a PAIR rather than rewriting one description in isolation.
repeats-are-not-replicates.measured: 12/18 pooled over 3 runs, Wilson [0.44, 0.84]; rnr-near 0/6 stable across all 3 runs

recorder-in-the-record.why: Round 405 (skills B) probed this as part of the seven-round owed batch: 41 cases, 205 probes, 0 errors, $11.97, four SEPARATE invocations (round-405-run{A,B,C,D}.json), canary in band 4/4 first. NO EDIT HAS BEEN MADE and round 141's stop-rule budget is untouched -- an edit changes the digest and throws the 205 probes away, and this round had no budget left to re-measure. REFUTED at 0 of 20 -- it fired ZERO times on all four of its positive cases in all four runs, Wilson 95% [0.00, 0.16]. It is one of two descriptions in this batch that never fired at all. The diagnosis is NOT a boundary problem and this is the sharpest instance in the corpus: 16 of its 20 losses were ABSTENTIONS (80%) -- no catalog skill fired at all -- and its top measured taker (echoed-record-vs-measurement) accounts for only 10% of them. There is no competitor to write a NOT-clause against; the description does not stake a claim the selector can act on. Its own negative case rir-neg-audit also false-fired 3 of 5, so it is not that the text is too narrow. The remedy the data supports is a concrete mechanism or symptom no neighbour could also claim -- see skills/losses-name-their-winner step 6. Do NOT pair it with echoed-record-vs-measurement. The next round to pick this up should re-derive rho first (round 405 measured 0.143 on 18 cases where round 393 measured 0.333 on 7) and spend the budget as N x --repeats 1 + ONE x --repeats 2, which is what keeps rho estimable at all.
recorder-in-the-record.measured: 0/20 pooled over 4 runs, Wilson [0.00, 0.16]; 16 of 20 losses were abstentions

run-the-comparison-you-suppress.why: Round 405 (skills B) probed this as part of the seven-round owed batch: 41 cases, 205 probes, 0 errors, $11.97, four SEPARATE invocations (round-405-run{A,B,C,D}.json), canary in band 4/4 first. NO EDIT HAS BEEN MADE and round 141's stop-rule budget is untouched -- an edit changes the digest and throws the 205 probes away, and this round had no budget left to re-measure. REFUTED at 0 of 20, Wilson 95% [0.00, 0.16] -- zero fires on all four positive cases in all four runs. Unlike recorder-in-the-record this IS a boundary problem and the boundary is not the one anyone named: only 2 of its 20 losses were abstentions, and `exemption-census` took 12 of them (60%), with measured-exemption taking 6 more. Round 401's registry entry insisted this be probed against `zero-rate-needs-a-distance` because the two 'overlap on the word exemption by construction' -- and that pairing is measurably a non-event: rcys-neg-zero, the crossing case, scores a clean 5/5. THE PAIR TO FIX IS THIS SKILL AND `exemption-census`, which nobody has named, and note that exemption-census itself is only 2 of 3 with a flaky case (P007). Round 393's finding still applies -- rewrite both sides at once or neither. The next round to pick this up should re-derive rho first (round 405 measured 0.143 on 18 cases where round 393 measured 0.333 on 7) and spend the budget as N x --repeats 1 + ONE x --repeats 2, which is what keeps rho estimable at all.
run-the-comparison-you-suppress.measured: 0/20 pooled over 4 runs, Wilson [0.00, 0.16]; 12 of 20 losses to exemption-census, 6 to measured-exemption, only 2 abstentions

instruments-already-running.why: Round 405 (skills B) probed this as part of the seven-round owed batch: 41 cases, 205 probes, 0 errors, $11.97, four SEPARATE invocations (round-405-run{A,B,C,D}.json), canary in band 4/4 first. NO EDIT HAS BEEN MADE and round 141's stop-rule budget is untouched -- an edit changes the digest and throws the 205 probes away, and this round had no budget left to re-measure. REFUTED at 6 of 25, Wilson 95% [0.11, 0.43]. The per-case pattern is stable and is NOT a draw: iar-near and iar-far scored 0/5 in every one of the four runs while iar-mid and iar-estimated scored 3/5 each, so two of its four cases are a real boundary failure and two are roughly a coin flip. 14 of its 19 losses (74%) were ABSTENTIONS; its top taker, lazy-fill-ceiling, accounts for 26%. Round 394's entry prescribed probing it against `residency-is-not-allocation` because their cases cross; measured, that pairing explains almost nothing -- and the crossing case kwyl-neg-instruments, which expects THIS skill, scored 0/5, i.e. the pair experiment could not have produced a signal because the named sibling is not in the room. Abstention-dominated: needs a claim, not a contrast. The next round to pick this up should re-derive rho first (round 405 measured 0.143 on 18 cases where round 393 measured 0.333 on 7) and spend the budget as N x --repeats 1 + ONE x --repeats 2, which is what keeps rho estimable at all.

untested-default-path.why: Round 405 (skills B) probed this as part of the seven-round owed batch: 41 cases, 205 probes, 0 errors, $11.97, four SEPARATE invocations (round-405-run{A,B,C,D}.json), canary in band 4/4 first. NO EDIT HAS BEEN MADE and round 141's stop-rule budget is untouched -- an edit changes the digest and throws the 205 probes away, and this round had no budget left to re-measure. REFUTED at 2 of 15, Wilson 95% [0.04, 0.38]. udp-far scored 0/5; udp-near and udp-mid fired once each out of five. Its losses are split: 5 of 13 abstentions, and the rest spread over echoed-record-vs-measurement (4), subprocess-cli-testing (3) and unrun-checker-latency (3) -- a top-taker share of 31%, which is diffuse enough that round 405's reading is the same as for an abstention (many different winners means no boundary exists, it means the subject is invisible). Round 395's entry named `unrun-checker-latency` and `derived-subject-set`; the first is a real but minority taker and the second never took one of its probes. Note the crossing case udp-neg, which expects unrun-checker-latency, scored a clean 5/5 -- the named sibling works fine when a case genuinely belongs to it, which is precisely the distinction that makes the naming useless for fixing THIS skill. The next round to pick this up should re-derive rho first (round 405 measured 0.143 on 18 cases where round 393 measured 0.333 on 7) and spend the budget as N x --repeats 1 + ONE x --repeats 2, which is what keeps rho estimable at all.
untested-default-path.measured: 2/15 pooled over 4 runs, Wilson [0.04, 0.38]; udp-far 0/5; losses 5 abstentions + a diffuse spread, top-taker share 31%

_round_375_note: Created by round 375 (skills B), closing the gap round 369 wrote into state/known-unprobed-skills.json's _round_369_note by name. The SIX P006 skills found this round -- fuzz-mutate-kill-loop (1 of 7), measured-exemption (1 of 3), unrun-checker-latency (1 of 3), deleted-vs-never-written / optimization-transparency-differential / pristine-checkout-differential (2 of 3) -- are deliberately NOT entered here. They are newly discovered and nobody has adjudicated them; an entry here means 'decided and carried', and pre-filling it with everything the checker found on its first run is how a baseline becomes the mute button its own rot check exists to prevent. They stay as live WARNINGs owed to the next skills(B) re-probe batch.
_round_381_note: Round 381 (skills B) DELETED the `measured-budget-sizing` entry and REWROTE `obligation-ledger`'s. Both were adjudicated `KNOWN-BAD description` from single 3-probe draws after a description edit failed to move them. Re-measured at the full 41-skill corpus at n=3 (state/trigger-eval/round-381-armJ.json): measured-budget-sizing 9/9, obligation-ledger 6/9. Staged alone (round-381-mbs-isolation.json / round-381-ol-isolation.json) both are 9/9. `measured-budget-sizing` had to go rather than be softened: at full recall an entry here is a P008 ERROR by this file's own rule, which is the rule working. The general finding is in knowledge/round-381-*.md -- two runs of the IDENTICAL configuration disagreed on 11 of 29 cases at majority level, and one skill read 0/12 in one run and 12/12, 4/4 and 11/12 in three others. Every verdict in this file that rests on ONE report is therefore suspect by construction, which is what the new P009 check now says out loud.
_round_405_note: Round 405 (skills B) added FOUR entries at once -- the four descriptions its 205-probe batch REFUTED (recorder-in-the-record 0/20, run-the-comparison-you-suppress 0/20, instruments-already-running 6/25, untested-default-path 2/15) -- and re-pinned derived-subject-set without changing its verdict. That is four new acknowledgements in one round, which is exactly the shape round 375's note warned about, so here is why each is a decision and not a mute button: all four were measured at n>=15 across FOUR independent runs with a canary in band, none was edited (round 141's stop-rule: an edit costs the 205 probes), and each `why` names the MEASURED taker and the abstention share rather than a plausible sibling. The general finding, which is what makes these entries actionable where the registry entries they replace were not: round 405 built skills/skill-authoring/scripts/displacement.py, the first instrument in this repo to ask what BEATS a losing skill rather than only whether it lost. 49% of losses in its own designed runs had no skill fire at all, and 0 of 5 descriptions that name a confusable had that named skill as their top measured taker. Two of these four entries are abstention-dominated (recorder-in-the-record 80%, instruments-already-running 74%) and want a CLAIM; one is displacement-dominated with a single clear rival (run-the-comparison-you-suppress -> exemption-census, 60%) and wants a paired BOUNDARY edit; one is diffuse (untested-default-path, top-taker 31%) and reads like the abstention cases. Those are three different remedies for what the corpus previously recorded as one number.
